result_text:
Suppliers now have payment terms in days. A new supplier defaults to 30 days, and `updateSupplier` changes them when renegotiated. The full suite passes offline (610 tests, including the new ones in `SupplierTest`). Nothing is committed.

What changed:

- **`schema.sql`**: `supplier` gets `payment_terms_days INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 30 CHECK (payment_terms_days >= 0)`.
- **`model/Supplier.java`**: new `int paymentTermsDays` component. I kept the old five-argument constructor as a delegating constructor that defaults to 30. That avoids touching the 78 existing call sites in tests and demo code.
- **`DataStore.java`**:
  - `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` write the terms.
  - All nine supplier read queries select the column and map it. That covers the four listings you named (by name, by country, by minimum rating, single lookup) and the other supplier queries too (purchase orders, spending, performance, stock per supplier, category suppliers). Without this, those would silently report 30.
- **`SupplierTest.java`**: tests for the 30-day default, the 45-then-14 renegotiation shown in every listing, and rejection of negative values. Negative values fail via the DB check, the same way ratings are validated.

There is no separate supplier service in this codebase, so `createSupplier` and `updateSupplier` on `DataStore` are the entry points.
